obligations.title: Upload monthly report on SEBI Intermediaries Portal within 7 working days of month end
obligations.summary: Registered Portfolio Managers must upload the monthly report on the SEBI Intermediaries Portal within 7 working days of the end of each month. No hard copy of the report needs to be sent to SEBI.

clause.excerpt: shall upload the report on SEBI Intermediaries Portal within 7 working days of the end of each month

control.name: Monthly report portal upload
control.description: A calendar-driven control that compiles the required monthly report and uploads it on the SEBI Intermediaries Portal within 7 working days of each month end, with the upload confirmation captured and tracked against the deadline.

evidenceSpec.description: SEBI Intermediaries Portal submission log or acknowledgement showing the report was uploaded for each month, with upload timestamps falling within 7 working days of the respective month end.

obligations.title: Submit limited Quarterly Activity Report on SI Portal within 15 days of quarter end
obligations.summary: All AIFs must file a limited Quarterly Activity Report online on the SI Portal in the prescribed format within 15 calendar days of each quarter end, with the first report covering the quarter ending June 2026. No separate filing is required for March quarters as the Annual Activity Report already contains those data points.

clause.excerpt: A limited Quarterly Activity Report shall be submitted by all AIFs online on the SI Portal in prescribed format within 15 calendar days from the end of each such quarter.

control.name: Quarterly Activity Report filing on SI Portal
control.description: Operate a quarterly reporting calendar that triggers preparation of the limited Quarterly Activity Report at each quarter end, compiles the prescribed data points, files the report online on the SI Portal, and logs the submission acknowledgement, ensuring filing within 15 calendar days of quarter end and skipping standalone March-quarter filings in favour of the Annual Activity Report.

evidenceSpec.description: Quarterly Activity Report in prescribed format together with the SI Portal submission acknowledgement for each applicable quarter
Submission log evidencing that each quarterly report was filed on the SI Portal within 15 calendar days of the quarter end, beginning with the quarter ending June 2026

obligations.title: File fresh registration application with SEBI within six months of prior approval
obligations.summary: Upon a change in control that has received prior approval, the portfolio manager must apply to SEBI for fresh registration within six months from the date of that prior approval.

clause.excerpt: Applications for fresh registration pursuant to change in control shall be made to SEBI within six months from the date of prior approval.

control.name: Change-in-control fresh registration filing
control.description: On receipt of SEBI prior approval for a change in control, record the approval date, prepare the fresh registration application, and submit it to SEBI with a computed six-month cut-off tracked via a compliance calendar so the filing occurs within the permitted window.

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the fresh registration application submitted to SEBI together with the SEBI submission acknowledgement or receipt
Register entry capturing the prior approval date, the computed six-month due date, and the actual filing date evidencing timely submission

obligations.title: Submit final approval application to SEBI within 15 days of NCLT order
obligations.summary: Within 15 calendar days of the NCLT order date, the Portfolio Manager must file an online application with SEBI for final approval, enclosing the NCLT order, approved scheme, statement of any modifications with reasons, and details of compliance with the in-principle approval conditions.

clause.excerpt: Within 15 [calendar] days from the date of order of NCLT, Portfolio Manager shall submit an online application in terms of paragraph 1.5.1.1 of this Master Circular along with the following documents to SEBI for final approval:

control.name: NCLT order final-approval filing control
control.description: Maintain a trigger that starts on the date of the NCLT order approving the scheme. Assemble the required enclosures (NCLT order, approved scheme, statement of modifications and reasons, compliance details against in-principle approval conditions), submit the online application on the SEBI portal in terms of paragraph 1.5.1.1, and record the submission date to verify it falls within 15 calendar days of the NCLT order.

evidenceSpec.description: SEBI portal submission acknowledgement for the final approval application, showing filing date and applicant entity

Bundle as filed: copy of the NCLT order approving the scheme, copy of the approved scheme, statement of modifications vis-a-vis the draft scheme with reasons, and details of compliance with conditions/observations in SEBI's in-principle approval
Computed date difference between the NCLT order date and the application submission date is 15 calendar days or fewer

obligations.title: Execute at least 10% of monthly CB secondary market trades via RFQ
obligations.summary: Each month, Portfolio Managers must route at least 10% of the total value of their secondary market corporate bond (CB) trades through the Request for Quote (RFQ) platform of stock exchanges, placing or seeking quotes in one-to-one (OTO) or one-to-many (OTM) mode.

clause.excerpt: Portfolio Managers shall undertake at least 10% of their total secondary market trades by value in CBs in that month by placing/seeking quotes through one-to-one (OTO) or one-to-many (OTM) mode on the Request for Quote platform of stock exchanges (RFQ)

control.name: Monthly RFQ execution ratio monitoring
control.description: At each month-end, compute total secondary market CB trade value for the month and the portion executed by placing/seeking quotes in OTO or OTM mode on the stock exchange RFQ platform; verify the RFQ-executed portion is at least 10% of total CB trade value, and remediate shortfalls before month-end close reporting.

evidenceSpec.description: Monthly reconciliation showing RFQ-executed CB trade value (OTO/OTM mode) against total secondary market CB trade value for the month, evidencing a ratio of at least 10%
Stock exchange RFQ platform trade/quote confirmations for OTO and OTM executions during the month

obligations.title: Rebalance portfolio within 90 days of passive investment limit breach
obligations.summary: When a passive breach of the specified investment limits occurs, the Portfolio Manager must complete rebalancing of the portfolio within 90 calendar days from the date of the breach. The client may instead give informed, prior positive consent to waive the rebalancing.

clause.excerpt: a rebalancing of the portfolio shall be completed by Portfolio Managers within a period of 90 [calendar] days from the date of such breach

control.name: Passive breach rebalancing monitor
control.description: Continuously monitor portfolio exposures against the specified investment limits; on detecting a passive breach, record the breach date, classify it as passive (not arising from omission or commission of the portfolio manager), and drive a rebalancing workflow tracked to completion within 90 calendar days; capture and store any informed, prior positive client consent where the client waives rebalancing.

evidenceSpec.description: Investment limit monitoring report showing the passive breach date and confirmation that portfolio rebalancing was completed on or before day 90 from that date
Rebalancing trade records or portfolio statements evidencing restoration of compliance, together with the client's written informed prior positive consent where rebalancing was waived

obligations.title: Submit annual compliance report to SEBI within 30 days of FY end
obligations.summary: Portfolio Managers must report to SEBI on their compliance with the guidelines when submitting annual reports. The report must reach SEBI within thirty calendar days from the end of the financial year.

clause.excerpt: Portfolio Managers shall report to SEBI on compliance with the provisions of the above guidelines while submitting the annual reports. The report should reach SEBI within thirty [calendar] days from the end of the financial year.

control.name: Annual compliance report preparation and submission
control.description: Prepare an annual compliance report against the guidelines at financial year end, obtain internal sign-off, and submit it to SEBI along with the annual reports such that it reaches SEBI within thirty calendar days of financial year end, with dispatch and acknowledgment records retained.

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the compliance report submitted to SEBI along with the annual reports
Submission acknowledgment or dispatch proof showing the report reached SEBI within thirty calendar days of financial year end

obligations.title: Follow APMI standard ToR for annual audit of firm-level performance data
obligations.summary: All Portfolio Managers must mandatorily follow the standard Terms of Reference specified by APMI, applicable with effect from October 01, 2023, when conducting the annual audit of firm-level performance data.

clause.excerpt: shall be mandatorily followed by all Portfolio Managers for the purpose of annual audit of firm-level performance data

control.name: Standard APMI ToR adoption for annual performance audit
control.description: Maintain the APMI standard Terms of Reference as the mandated scope document for the annual audit of firm-level performance data; ensure every annual audit engagement issued to the auditor incorporates the standard ToR without deviation and that the audit is executed against it.

evidenceSpec.description: Annual audit engagement letter or auditor mandate referencing the APMI standard ToR for firm-level performance data audit
Completed annual audit report on firm-level performance data confirming the audit was performed per the APMI standard ToR

obligations.title: Submit quarterly client data in specified formats within 15 days of quarter end
obligations.summary: Portfolio Managers must submit data in the specified formats for all clients every quarter within 15 calendar days of quarter end. Day-wise data must be furnished for the 'Client Folio AUM' and 'Client Holding Master' table headings.

clause.excerpt: Portfolio Managers shall submit data as per the specified formats for all its clients on quarterly basis within [15 calendar days]78from end of the quarter. Day-wise data shall be furnished for table headings: “Client Folio AUM” and “Client Holding Master”.

control.name: Quarterly client data submission
control.description: Generate client-level data in the prescribed table formats for all clients each quarter, ensure day-wise detail for Client Folio AUM and Client Holding Master headings, and transmit the submission within 15 calendar days of quarter end.

evidenceSpec.description: Quarterly submission files in the specified format covering all clients, including day-wise data for 'Client Folio AUM' and 'Client Holding Master' headings
Submission log evidencing each quarterly file was transmitted within 15 calendar days from end of the quarter

obligations.title: Furnish quarterly report to clients in Annexure 5D format
obligations.summary: Portfolio Managers must provide each of their clients with a report in the format prescribed at Annexure 5D of the Master Circular, on a quarterly basis.

clause.excerpt: Portfolio Managers shall furnish a report in the format provided at Annexure 5D81 of this Master Circular, to their clients on a quarterly basis 82 which inter-alia includes the following:

control.name: Quarterly client report generation and dispatch
control.description: Each quarter, compile the client report in the prescribed Annexure 5D format from portfolio records, review it for completeness against the template, and dispatch it to every client, logging the dispatch date and recipient for each client.

evidenceSpec.description: Copies of the quarterly client reports issued in the Annexure 5D format for the period under review
Dispatch log reconciling every active client with a quarterly report sent, including dates of dispatch

obligations.title: Verify all performance statistics in the annual audit
obligations.summary: All performance statistics referred to in the preceding provisions must be verified as part of the annual audit conducted under the Regulations.

clause.excerpt: Verification of all the above performance statistics shall be carried out in the annual audit under the Regulations.

control.name: Annual audit verification of performance statistics
control.description: Each year, the firm ensures the annual audit under the Regulations covers verification of every performance statistic it reports, with the auditor checking the computed figures against underlying records and documenting the verification outcome.

evidenceSpec.description: Annual audit report or auditor's verification annex confirming that all performance statistics were verified, including the period covered and the statistics checked.

obligations.title: Submit monthly reports to APMI in addition to SEBI within 7 working days of month-end
obligations.summary: Each month, the Portfolio Manager must file its monthly report with APMI as well as with SEBI, completing the APMI submission within 7 working days from the end of that month.

clause.excerpt: Portfolio Managers shall also submit the monthly reports to APMI in addition to SEBI within 7 working days from the end of each month.

control.name: APMI monthly report filing control
control.description: A month-end compliance calendar item that triggers preparation of the monthly report and its submission to APMI (in parallel with the SEBI filing), with the due date tracked as month-end plus 7 working days and escalation for any report not filed in time.

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the monthly report as submitted to APMI, together with APMI submission acknowledgement or receipt
Filing log recording the APMI submission date for each monthly report, confirming submission occurred within 7 working days of the relevant month-end

obligations.title: Compute performance fee using high water mark principle
obligations.summary: Performance/profit sharing fee shall be computed on the basis of the high water mark principle over the life of the investment, where the high water mark is the highest value the portfolio/account has reached.

clause.excerpt: Profit/ performance shall be computed on the basis of high water mark principle over the life of the investment, for charging of performance / profit sharing fee.

control.name: High Water Mark computation
control.description: Maintain a rolling record of the highest portfolio value achieved over the life of each investment and compute performance fee only on gains above that mark.

evidenceSpec.description: Fee calculation records showing high water mark values and fee charged only on excess returns for each client account

obligations.title: Value portfolio for high water mark on performance fee charge date
obligations.summary: The value of the portfolio used for computation of the high water mark shall be the value on the date when performance fees are charged.

clause.excerpt: Value of the portfolio for computation of high watermark shall be taken to be the value on the date when performance fees are charged.

control.name: Valuation at fee charge date
control.description: System captures the portfolio valuation on the fee charge date and uses it as the high water mark computation input.

evidenceSpec.description: Valuation snapshots on fee charge dates linked to high water mark calculations

obligations.title: Charge performance fees at least quarterly
obligations.summary: For the purpose of charging performance fee, the frequency shall not be less than quarterly.

clause.excerpt: For the purpose of charging performance fee, the frequency shall not be less than quarterly.

control.name: Fee charging frequency check
control.description: Policy and system configuration ensure performance fees are charged no less frequently than quarterly.

evidenceSpec.description: Fee charging policy stating minimum quarterly frequency
Fee charging log showing intervals between performance fee charges

obligations.title: Charge performance fee only on gains above previous high water mark
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager shall charge performance based fee only on increase in portfolio value in excess of the previously achieved high water mark.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall charge performance based fee only on increase in portfolio value in excess of the previously achieved high water mark.

control.name: Excess-return fee gate
control.description: Fee engine compares current portfolio value against previously achieved high water mark and permits fee only on the excess, blocking fees when value is below the mark.

evidenceSpec.description: Fee computations demonstrating fees charged only on value in excess of prior high water mark, including periods of decline

obligations.title: Monthly website disclosure of complaint data including SCORES complaints
obligations.summary: Portfolio Managers must publish on their websites, every month, data on all complaints received, including SCORES complaints, in the format prescribed in Annexure 7A of the Master Circular.

clause.excerpt: all Portfolio Managers on a monthly basis shall disclose on their websites, the data pertaining to all complaints including SCORES complaints received by them in the format mentioned in Annexure 7A of this Master Circular

control.name: Monthly investor complaint disclosure upload
control.description: Each month, compile the complaint data (including SCORES complaints) in the Annexure 7A format, obtain internal sign-off, and publish it on the firm's website on or before the 7th of the succeeding month, with an archive of each published disclosure retained.

evidenceSpec.description: Archived copy or screenshot of the website page showing the monthly complaint data disclosure in Annexure 7A format, dated for the reporting month.
Publication log confirming the disclosure was made available on the website by the 7th of the succeeding month for each reporting period.

obligations.title: Maintain investor complaint data per Annexure 5, compiled within 7 days of quarter end
obligations.summary: AIFs must maintain data on investor complaints in the Annexure 5 format and compile it no later than 7 days after the end of each quarter for effective monitoring.

clause.excerpt: For effective monitoring, AIFs shall maintain data on investor complaints as per Annexure 5, which shall be compiled latest within 7 days from the end of quarter.

control.name: Quarterly investor complaint data compilation
control.description: Maintain a live register of investor complaints capturing the fields prescribed in Annexure 5 throughout the quarter; at quarter close, compile the data and confirm the compilation is completed within 7 days of quarter end before review and submission.

evidenceSpec.description: Completed Annexure 5 investor complaint data compilation for the quarter, timestamped within 7 days of quarter end
Investor complaint register validated against Annexure 5 field requirements for completeness and accuracy at each quarter close

obligations.title: Execute at least 10% of monthly corporate bond secondary trades via RFQ platform
obligations.summary: AIFs must ensure that at least 10% of the value of their total secondary market trades in Corporate Bonds each month is undertaken by placing or seeking quotes on the RFQ platform.

clause.excerpt: AIFs shall undertake at least 10% of their total secondary market trades in Corporate Bonds by value in a month by placing/seeking quotes on the RFQ platform.

control.name: RFQ execution threshold monitor
control.description: At each month-end, reconcile the total value of secondary market trades in Corporate Bonds against the value of such trades executed by placing or seeking quotes on the RFQ platform, and verify that the RFQ-executed proportion is at least 10%; escalate and remediate any shortfall.

evidenceSpec.description: Monthly reconciliation report showing total secondary market Corporate Bond trade value for the month and the value executed via RFQ quotes, demonstrating the at-least-10% threshold is met.
RFQ platform trade/quote records (or broker-provided RFQ execution logs) for the month supporting the reconciliation.

obligations.title: Furnish overseas divestment details to SEBI within 3 working days
obligations.summary: AIFs must report the sale/divestment details of their overseas investments to SEBI in the Annexure 9 format by emailing aifreporting@sebi.gov.in within 3 working days of the divestment, so that the overall limit available for overseas investment by AIFs is updated.

clause.excerpt: AIFs shall furnish the sale/divestment details of the overseas investments to SEBI in the format given at Annexure 9 within 3 working days of the divestment, by emailing to aifreporting@sebi.gov.in, for updating the overall limit available for overseas investment by AIFs.

control.name: Overseas divestment reporting control
control.description: Maintain a log of every sale/divestment of an overseas investment. On each divestment event, compile the sale details in the Annexure 9 format and email them to aifreporting@sebi.gov.in within 3 working days of the divestment, with a tracker confirming timely dispatch for each event.

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the email sent to aifreporting@sebi.gov.in containing the completed Annexure 9 divestment details, with sent-date evidencing dispatch within 3 working days of divestment
Reconciliation of the overseas divestment log against SEBI reporting emails, confirming every divestment has a corresponding Annexure 9 submission made within 3 working days

obligations.title: Upload latest NAV per unit ISIN to depository system within 30 days of valuation
obligations.summary: AIFs, acting through their RTAs, must upload the latest available NAV for each ISIN of AIF units into the depository system within 30 days from the date the investment portfolio is valued.

clause.excerpt: AIFs, through their RTAs, shall upload the latest available NAV corresponding to each ISIN of units of the AIF in the depository system within 30 days from the date of valuation of the investment portfolio.

control.name: NAV upload tracking within 30-day window
control.description: After each portfolio valuation, capture the valuation date and the latest NAV per ISIN, trigger the RTA upload of these NAVs into the depository system, and monitor each ISIN's upload against the 30-day window from the valuation date, escalating any ISIN not uploaded in time.

evidenceSpec.description: Depository system record showing, for each ISIN of AIF units, the uploaded NAV value and upload timestamp, reconciled to fall within 30 days of the corresponding portfolio valuation date.
RTA upload confirmation or upload log listing each ISIN, its NAV, the valuation date and the date of upload to the depository system.

obligations.title: Submit final approval documents to SEBI within 15 days of NCLT order
obligations.summary: Once the NCLT passes its order on the scheme, the applicant must apply to SEBI for final approval within 15 days of the order date, enclosing the NCLT order, the approved scheme, a statement of any modifications vis-à-vis the draft scheme with reasons, and details of compliance with the conditions or observations in SEBI's in-principle approval.

clause.excerpt: Within 15 days from the date of order of NCLT, applicant shall submit the following documents to SEBI for final approval: (i) Application for the final approval; (ii) Copy of the NCLT Order approving the scheme; (iii) Copy of the approved scheme; (iv) Statement explaining modifications, if any, in the approved scheme vis-à-vis the draft scheme and the reasons for the same; and (v) Details of compliance with the conditions/ observations mentioned in the in- principle approval provided by SEBI.

control.name: NCLT-order final approval filing
control.description: On receipt of the NCLT order approving the scheme, a designated owner compiles the final approval application pack — application form, NCLT order, approved scheme, modification statement with reasons, and a compliance mapping against each condition or observation in SEBI's in-principle approval — and files it with SEBI within 15 days of the NCLT order date, tracking the clock from the order date to submission.

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the final approval application submitted to SEBI with all five enclosures (application, NCLT order, approved scheme, modification statement, compliance details)
Record showing the SEBI submission date is within 15 days of the NCLT order date

obligations.title: Ensure agreements require investor reporting of internal policy changes
obligations.summary: Where an investor has disclosed that participation in the investment opportunity would contravene its internal policy, the manager must ensure the terms of the agreement with that investor include a requirement to report any change in the disclosed internal policy to the AIF within 15 days of the change.

clause.excerpt: Manager shall ensure that terms of such agreement with the investor include reporting of any change in the disclosed internal policy, to the AIF, within 15 days of such change.

control.name: Contract clause verification for internal policy change reporting
control.description: Fund contracting and onboarding process ensures that any contribution agreement or other agreement with an investor who has disclosed an internal-policy contravention contains a term obliging the investor to notify the AIF of any change in that disclosed policy within 15 days; executed agreements are reviewed against a clause checklist before acceptance.

evidenceSpec.description: Executed contribution or other agreement containing the clause requiring the investor to report changes in the disclosed internal policy to the AIF within 15 days
Contract review checklist confirming every qualifying investor agreement includes the internal-policy change reporting term with the 15-day window

obligations.title: Obtain investor approval before each investment in associates or related AIF units
obligations.summary: Before making any investment in an associate, or in units of an AIF managed or sponsored by the Manager, Sponsor or their associates, the AIF must obtain the specified approval of its investors.

clause.excerpt: prior to every investment in an associate or in units of an AIF managed or sponsored by Manager, Sponsor or associates of Manager or Sponsor, approval of the investors as specified shall be obtained.

control.name: Pre-investment investor approval gate for related-party investments
control.description: Maintain a screening step in the investment approval workflow that flags any proposed investment in an associate or in units of an AIF managed or sponsored by the Manager, Sponsor or their associates, and blocks execution until the investor approval specified under Regulation 15(1)(e) has been obtained and recorded.

evidenceSpec.description: Signed investor approval or consent record (in the specified form) obtained prior to the investment, filed against the related-party investment.

Report listing every investment in an associate or in AIF units managed/sponsored by the Manager, Sponsor or their associates, each linked to a dated investor approval record timestamped before the investment date.
Deal-pipeline scan flagging any proposed transaction with an associate or related AIF that lacks a recorded pre-investment investor approval.

obligations.title: Annual disclosure of PPM changes to SEBI and investors
obligations.summary: The AIF manager must annually submit, as part of changes in the PPM to SEBI and investors, details of any changes in valuation methodology for each asset class of the scheme, changes in accounting practices/policies of the investee company and the scheme, and the impact of those changes on the valuation of the scheme's investments.

clause.excerpt: The manager shall disclose the following as part of changes in PPM to be submitted annually to SEBI and investors:

control.name: Annual PPM change disclosure control
control.description: Maintain a change register capturing any changes during the year in valuation methodology and approach for each asset class of the scheme and in accounting practices/policies of the investee company and the scheme; assess the valuation impact of each change; compile the three disclosure items into the annual PPM-change submission filed with SEBI and circulated to investors.

evidenceSpec.description: Annual PPM-change submission to SEBI (with filing acknowledgement) and record of circulation to investors, covering disclosure items (a), (b) and (c).
Change register for the reporting year listing valuation methodology and accounting policy changes per asset class and investee company, each mapped to its stated valuation impact.

obligations.title: Exercise specific due diligence to prevent circumvention of specified laws
obligations.summary: The AIF, its Manager and Key Management Personnel must carry out specific due diligence on the AIF's investors and investments to prevent facilitation of circumvention of laws specified by SEBI from time to time.

clause.excerpt: every AIF, Manager of the AIF and Key Management Personnel of the Manager and the AIF shall exercise specific due diligence, with respect to investors and investments of the AIF, to prevent facilitation of circumvention of such laws, as may be specified by SEBI from time to time.

control.name: Anti-circumvention due diligence over investors and investments
control.description: Operate documented due diligence procedures that screen the AIF's investors and investments for arrangements that could facilitate circumvention of laws specified by SEBI, and update the screening as SEBI specifies additional laws.

evidenceSpec.description: Documented due diligence policy and procedures covering investor and investment screening for circumvention risk
Due diligence screening records for investors and investments showing checks performed, findings and outcomes

obligations.title: Conduct due diligence per SFA standards before SR investments or QB benefits
obligations.summary: For every AIF scheme where a single investor or investors belonging to the same group contribute 50 percent or more of the scheme corpus, necessary due diligence as per the implementation standards formulated by SFA must be carried out. This must be completed prior to making any investments in SRs issued by ARCs or availing benefits designated for QBs under the SARFAESI Act.

clause.excerpt: For every scheme of AIFs having an investor, or investors belonging to the same group, who contribute(s) 50 percent or more to the corpus of the scheme, necessary due diligence as per the implementation standards formulated by SFA, shall be carried out prior to making any investments in SRs issued by ARCs or availing benefits designated for QBs under the SARFAESI Act.

control.name: Pre-investment SFA due diligence gate
control.description: Before executing any investment in security receipts issued by ARCs or before availing QB benefits under the SARFAESI Act, the fund accounting/compliance team checks whether the scheme has an investor, or investors of the same group, contributing 50 percent or more of the corpus. If so, the due diligence prescribed in the SFA implementation standards is completed and signed off, and the transaction is blocked until that sign-off is on record.

evidenceSpec.description: Completed and signed due diligence report or checklist prepared per the SFA implementation standards, dated before the SR investment or QB benefit was availed
Corpus concentration report identifying each scheme where an investor or a same-group investor set holds 50 percent or more of the scheme corpus, triggering the due diligence requirement

obligations.title: Submit Annual Activity Report within 30 calendar days of end of March
obligations.summary: Every AIF must file a comprehensive Annual Activity Report online on the SEBI Intermediary Portal (SI Portal), within 30 calendar days from the end of March of each financial year.

clause.excerpt: AIFs shall submit a comprehensive Annual Activity Report at the end of March of each financial year. The Annual Activity Report shall be submitted by all AIFs online on the SEBI Intermediary Portal (SI Portal) within 30 calendar days from the end of March of every financial year.

control.name: Annual Activity Report filing control
control.description: Each financial year, compile the comprehensive Annual Activity Report covering the AIF's activities and submit it online through the SEBI Intermediary Portal no later than 30 calendar days after 31 March, with a tracked calendar trigger and maker-checker review before filing.

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the Annual Activity Report as submitted on the SI Portal for the relevant financial year
SI Portal submission acknowledgement showing the filing date fell within 30 calendar days of the end of March

obligations.title: Submit annual CTR within 30 days of financial year end to trustee/sponsor
obligations.summary: The AIF must submit the CTR within 30 days from the end of each financial year. It goes to the trustee and sponsor if the AIF is a trust, and to the sponsor alone if the AIF is set up in any other form.

clause.excerpt: The CTR shall be submitted within 30 days from the end of the financial year, to (a) the trustee and sponsor, in case the AIF is a trust; (b) the sponsor, in case of AIF set up in the form other than a trust.

control.name: Annual CTR preparation and distribution control
control.description: Maintain a calendar trigger at financial year end to prepare the CTR and dispatch it within 30 days, with recipient routing determined by the AIF's legal form (trustee and sponsor for trusts, sponsor only for other structures), and log dispatch and acknowledgement for each recipient.

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the submitted CTR together with delivery acknowledgements showing dispatch to the trustee and sponsor (for trusts) or the sponsor (for other structures).
Submission log recording the CTR dispatch date within 30 days of financial year end and the recipients matched to the AIF's legal form.

obligations.title: Conduct annual audit of compliance with PPM terms
obligations.summary: The AIF must have an audit carried out at the end of each financial year to verify compliance with the terms of its private placement memorandum.

clause.excerpt: Audit of compliance with terms of PPM, shall be conducted at the end of each Financial Year

control.name: Annual PPM compliance audit
control.description: At each financial year-end, commission an audit (internal or external) that tests the fund's activities, disclosures and operations against the commitments made in the PPM, and document the scope, findings and any corrective steps arising.

evidenceSpec.description: Signed PPM compliance audit report for the financial year, including findings and corrective steps
Audit calendar or tracker showing the audit was completed at the end of each financial year

obligations.title: Communicate PPM audit findings and corrective steps to governance bodies and SEBI
obligations.summary: The audit findings, along with any corrective steps, must be sent to the Trustee or Board of Directors or Designated Partners of the AIF, the Board of directors or Designated Partners of the Manager, and SEBI within six months of the end of the financial year.

clause.excerpt: the findings of audit along with corrective steps, if any, shall be communicated to the Trustee or Board of Directors or Designated Partners of the AIF, Board of directors or Designated Partners of the Manager and SEBI, within 6 months from the end of the Financial Year.

control.name: Audit findings distribution workflow
control.description: After each annual PPM compliance audit, compile the findings and corrective steps and dispatch them to the AIF's Trustee/Board/Designated Partners, the Manager's Board/Designated Partners, and SEBI, ensuring dispatch occurs within six months of financial year end.

evidenceSpec.description: Copies of the communications transmitting audit findings and corrective steps to each recipient, including SEBI
Dispatch log recording recipients and send dates, confirming delivery within six months of financial year end

obligations.title: Intimate changes in PPM and fund documents to investors and SEBI annually
obligations.summary: Any changes in the terms of the PPM and in the documents of the fund/scheme must be intimated to investors and SEBI on a consolidated basis within one month of the end of each Financial Year, specifically mentioning the changes made along with relevant pages of revised sections/clauses.

clause.excerpt: Any changes in terms of PPM and in the documents of the fund/scheme shall be intimated to investors and SEBI on a consolidated basis, within 1 month of the end of each Financial Year.

control.name: Annual PPM change intimation
control.description: Maintain a change log of all PPM and fund/scheme document changes during the financial year; at year-end, compile a consolidated intimation specifying each change with relevant pages of revised sections/clauses and dispatch it to investors and SEBI within one month of financial year end.

evidenceSpec.description: Consolidated annual intimation letter listing PPM and fund document changes, with revised section/clause pages, sent to investors and SEBI
Proof of dispatch to investors and filing/acknowledgement from SEBI within 1 month of financial year end

obligations.title: Report scheme-wise cash flow and valuation data to Benchmarking Agencies
obligations.summary: AIFs must submit data on cash flows and valuation of scheme-wise investments to each Benchmarking Agency in its required form and format within 45 days of the September 30 half-year end and within 7 months of the March 31 half-year end, including valuation principles and the Valuation Agency's name.

clause.excerpt: AIFs shall provide data on cash flows and valuation of their scheme-wise investments to the Benchmarking Agencies in the form and format required by each Benchmarking Agency, within 45 days from the end of every half-year ending on September 30 and within 7 months from the end of every half-year ending on March 31.

control.name: Half-yearly benchmarking data submission
control.description: Maintain a calendar for the two half-year cycles; compile scheme-wise cash flow and valuation data, valuation principles, and Valuation Agency name; format per each Benchmarking Agency's specification; validate and submit within 45 days (Sep 30 cycle) or 7 months (Mar 31 cycle).

evidenceSpec.description: Submission acknowledgement or receipt from each Benchmarking Agency for each half-year period
Log recording submission date versus deadline (45 days / 7 months) for each reporting cycle, confirming inclusion of valuation principles and Valuation Agency name

obligations.title: Submit audited data as of March 31 and data as of September 30
obligations.summary: When reporting data, the figures provided as of March 31 each year must be audited, while figures as of September 30 may be unaudited.

clause.excerpt: Data provided for March 31 of every year shall be audited data and for September 30 may be unaudited data.

control.name: Periodic data audit assurance control
control.description: Maintain a reporting calendar ensuring March 31 data is drawn only from audited financials, with sign-off that audited statements have been obtained before submission; September 30 data may be sourced from management accounts.

evidenceSpec.description: Audited financial statements as of March 31 for the reporting year
Checklist confirming March 31 figures reconcile to audited accounts and September 30 figures are flagged as audited or unaudited

obligations.title: Include audited-accounts timeframe in investee agreements
obligations.summary: The Manager of an AIF must include a specific timeframe for the investee company to provide audited accounts to the AIF in the subscription agreement or investment agreement, enabling valuation reporting on audited data as on March 31.

clause.excerpt: Manager of AIF shall ensure that a specific timeframe for providing audited accounts by the investee company to the AIF is included as one of the terms in subscription agreement / investment agreement with the investee company

control.name: Investee agreement audited-accounts clause
control.description: Template check ensuring every subscription or investment agreement executed with an investee company contains a contractual timeframe for delivery of audited accounts to the AIF.

evidenceSpec.description: Executed subscription/investment agreements or signed addenda showing the audited-accounts provision timeframe clause

obligations.title: Report audited valuations only after AIF audit under Reg 20(14)
obligations.summary: The Manager of an AIF must ensure that valuation based on audited data of the investee company is reported to performance benchmarking agencies only after completion of the audit of the AIF's books of accounts under Regulation 20(14), within stipulated timelines.

clause.excerpt: Manager of AIF shall ensure that valuation based on audited data of investee company is reported to performance benchmarking agencies only after the audit of books of accounts of the AIF in terms of Regulation 20(14) of AIF Regulations, within the stipulated timelines

control.name: Pre-reporting audit completion gate
control.description: Sequencing control that blocks submission of audited-data valuations to the benchmarking agency until the AIF's annual audit under Regulation 20(14) is complete.

evidenceSpec.description: Signed AIF audit report or auditor completion certificate under Regulation 20(14), dated before the benchmarking submission

obligations.title: Submit compliance report on SEBI Intermediary Portal after exercising option
obligations.summary: The AIF manager, upon exercising any option under the circular, must file a compliance report on the SEBI Intermediary Portal in the specified format and/or as part of quarterly regulatory reporting to SEBI.

clause.excerpt: shall submit report on compliance with the provisions of this circular on SEBI Intermediary Portal in the format as specified therein and/or as part of quarterly regulatory reporting to SEBI, as the case may be

control.name: Compliance report submission upon option exercise
control.description: When the manager exercises any option under the circular, trigger preparation of the compliance report in the prescribed format and file it on the SEBI Intermediary Portal and/or include it in quarterly regulatory reporting to SEBI, as applicable.

evidenceSpec.description: Submitted compliance report on SEBI Intermediary Portal in the specified format
Quarterly regulatory report to SEBI containing the compliance disclosure

obligations.title: Submit annual status report on retained monies and outstanding liabilities
obligations.summary: AIFs with schemes that have retained monies and AIFs tagged as 'Inoperative Funds' must file an annual status report on retained monies and outstanding liabilities with SEBI and send it to investors of the relevant scheme(s), in the Annexure 23 format. The report must be submitted on the SEBI Intermediary portal within 30 calendar days from the end of March of every financial year.

clause.excerpt: shall submit an annual status report on retained monies and outstanding liabilities to SEBI and to investors of the relevant scheme(s), in the format as given at Annexure 23 of this circular. The report shall be submitted on SEBI Intermediary portal within 30 calendar days from the end of March of every financial year.

control.name: Annual retained monies status report filing
control.description: Each financial year, compile the Annexure 23 status report covering retained monies and outstanding liabilities for each in-scope scheme, obtain internal review and sign-off, file it on the SEBI Intermediary portal within 30 calendar days of the end of March, and dispatch the same report to investors of the relevant scheme(s).

evidenceSpec.description: Annual status report in Annexure 23 format as filed on the SEBI Intermediary portal, together with the portal submission acknowledgement showing the filing date
Record of dispatch of the status report to investors of the relevant scheme(s), such as an email distribution log or investor communication record
Portal acknowledgement timestamp confirms submission occurred within 30 calendar days of the end of March

obligations.title: Ensure existing fund-management decision-makers pass NISM-Series-XXI-B within two years
obligations.summary: Portfolio Managers must ensure that associated persons who are principal officers or employees with decision-making authority related to fund management as on the notification date obtain the NISM-Series-XXI-B: Portfolio Managers Certification Examination certification within two years from the date of the notification.

clause.excerpt: The Portfolio Managers shall ensure that all such associated persons who are principal officers or employees having decision making authority related to fund management as on the date of this notification obtain the certification by passing the NISM-Series-XXI-B: Portfolio Managers Certification Examination within two years from the date of the notification

control.name: Existing personnel certification completion tracking
control.description: Maintain a register of all principal officers and employees having fund-management decision-making authority as on the notification date, enrol each for the NISM-Series-XXI-B examination, track pass status against the two-year window from the notification date, and escalate for any person approaching the deadline uncertified.

evidenceSpec.description: Register of in-scope associated persons (principal officers and employees with fund-management decision-making authority) with NISM-Series-XXI-B certificate copies or NISM certification verification records
Report showing all personnel existing as on the notification date hold valid NISM-Series-XXI-B certification within two years of the notification date, with exceptions flagged

obligations.title: Ensure new fund-management decision-makers pass NISM-Series-XXI-B within one year
obligations.summary: Where a Portfolio Manager engages or employs a principal officer or employee with decision-making authority related to fund management after the date of Gazette Notification No. SEBI/LAD-NRO/GN/2021/49, the Portfolio Manager must ensure that person passes the NISM-Series-XXI-B certification within one year from the date of employment.

clause.excerpt: a Portfolio Manager, who engages or employs any such associated person who is a principal officer or an employee having decision making authority related to fund management, after the date of the Gazette Notification No. SEBI/LAD-NRO/GN/2021/49, shall ensure that such person obtains certification by passing the NISM- Series-XXI-B: Portfolio Managers Certification Examination within one year from the date of their employment

control.name: New hire certification compliance tracking
control.description: On engagement or employment of any principal officer or employee with fund-management decision-making authority, record the employment date, flag the person in the certification tracker, and monitor pass status of the NISM-Series-XXI-B examination to ensure completion within one year of employment.

evidenceSpec.description: Employment or engagement records with joining dates for principal officers and fund-management decision-makers engaged after the Gazette Notification date, together with their NISM-Series-XXI-B certificates
Exception report listing any newly engaged in-scope person who has not passed the NISM-Series-XXI-B examination within one year of their employment date

obligations.title: Ensure existing PMS distributors pass NISM-Series-XXI-A exam within two years
obligations.summary: Portfolio managers must ensure that every associated person who is a distributor of Portfolio Management Services as on the date of the notification obtains the NISM-Series-XXI-A: PMS Distributors Certification by passing the examination within two years from the date of the notification.

clause.excerpt: The Portfolio Managers shall ensure that all such associated persons who are distributors of the Portfolio Management Services as on the date of the notification obtain the certification by passing the NISM- Series-XXI-A: Portfolio Management Services (PMS) Distributors Certification Examination within two years from the date of the notification

control.name: Existing distributor certification tracker
control.description: Maintain a register of all associated persons acting as PMS distributors as on the notification date, record each person's NISM-Series-XXI-A examination status, and escalate to ensure every uncertified distributor passes the examination within two years of the notification date.

evidenceSpec.description: Register of associated persons who are PMS distributors as on the notification date, with NISM-Series-XXI-A examination status and pass date for each person
NISM-Series-XXI-A: PMS Distributors Certification Examination pass certificates for all in-scope associated persons

obligations.title: Ensure newly engaged PMS distributors pass NISM-Series-XXI-A exam within one year
obligations.summary: A portfolio manager who engages or employs a new associated person as a PMS distributor after the date of the notification must ensure that person passes the NISM-Series-XXI-A: PMS Distributors Certification Examination within one year from the date of their employment.

clause.excerpt: shall ensure that such person obtains certification by passing the NISM-Series-XXI-A: Portfolio Management Services (PMS) Distributors Certification Examination within one year from the date of their employment

control.name: New distributor onboarding certification check
control.description: On engaging or employing any associated person as a PMS distributor after the notification date, log the employment date, flag the person for mandatory certification, and track that the NISM-Series-XXI-A examination is passed within one year of the employment date, with escalation before the window lapses.

evidenceSpec.description: Log of associated persons engaged or employed as PMS distributors after the notification date, showing employment date and NISM-Series-XXI-A pass date within one year of employment
NISM-Series-XXI-A examination pass certificate for each newly engaged or employed PMS distributor

obligations.title: Maintain accounting system with separate client-wise data for funds
obligations.summary: Portfolio Managers must operate an accounting system that keeps client-wise data for their funds segregated for each client.

clause.excerpt: maintain an accounting system containing separate client-wise data for their funds

control.name: Client-wise fund accounting segregation
control.description: Operate an accounting system in which funds are recorded under separate client-wise data for each client, with checks that no client's funds data is commingled with another's.

evidenceSpec.description: Accounting system records or configuration demonstrating separate client-wise data for each client's funds

obligations.title: Provide monthly account statements to clients
obligations.summary: Portfolio Managers must furnish clients with statements for their segregated accounts at least once every month.

clause.excerpt: provide statement to clients for such accounts at least on monthly basis

control.name: Monthly client account statement generation and dispatch
control.description: Each month, generate account statements from the client-wise accounting system and dispatch them to every client, with a completeness check confirming no active client was skipped in the cycle.

evidenceSpec.description: Sample monthly client account statements with dispatch or delivery logs
Monthly dispatch report showing statements issued to all active clients

obligations.title: Submit audited firm-level performance data report to SEBI annually
obligations.summary: Portfolio Managers must have their firm-level performance data audited and submit the audit report to SEBI within 60 calendar days of the end of each financial year.

clause.excerpt: Portfolio Managers shall submit audit report on firm-level performance data to SEBI within sixty [calendar] days from end of each financial year.

control.name: Annual performance data audit and SEBI filing
control.description: At each financial year-end, commission an audit of firm-level performance data, obtain the signed audit report, and submit it to SEBI within 60 calendar days of the financial year-end, tracking the filing through to acknowledged submission.

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the signed audit report on firm-level performance data for the relevant financial year
Proof of submission of the audit report to SEBI (filing acknowledgement or email receipt) dated within 60 calendar days of financial year-end

obligations.title: Declare First Close of scheme within 12 months of launch eligibility
obligations.summary: For each scheme, the AIF must declare the First Close no later than 12 months from the date the AIF becomes eligible to launch that scheme under para 2.4.1 of the Master circular.

clause.excerpt: The First Close of a scheme shall be declared not later than 12 months from the date on which the AIF becomes eligible to launch its scheme as stated at para 2.4.1 of this Master circular.

control.name: First Close deadline tracking
control.description: Maintain a scheme-level compliance register that records the date the AIF becomes eligible to launch each scheme (per para 2.4.1), computes the 12-month First Close deadline, and tracks the declaration of First Close against it, with escalation if the deadline approaches unmet.

evidenceSpec.description: Register entry per scheme showing the eligibility-to-launch date, the computed 12-month deadline, and the actual First Close declaration date confirming the deadline was met.
The First Close declaration or notice issued for the scheme, together with board or investment committee approval evidencing the declaration.

obligations.title: Provide exit option to dissenting unit holders on material changes
obligations.summary: On material changes significantly influencing investors' decision to remain invested, existing unit holders who do not wish to continue must be provided an exit option, with not less than one month to express their dissent.

clause.excerpt: Existing unit holders who do not wish to continue post the change shall be provided an exit option. The unit holders shall be provided not less than one month for expressing their dissent.

control.name: Dissent exit mechanism
control.description: On identifying a material change, notify unit holders, offer an exit option, and keep the dissent window open for at least one month.

evidenceSpec.description: Communication to unit holders announcing the material change and exit option, with dissent window dates
Record of dissenting unit holders and exit offers made within the one-month window

obligations.title: Provide exit for close-ended schemes with dual independent valuation
obligations.summary: For close-ended schemes, exit shall be by buying out dissenting investors' units, and prior to buy-out the units shall be valued by two independent valuers, with exit at a value not less than the average of the two valuations.

clause.excerpt: Prior to buying out of such units, valuation of the units shall be undertaken by two independent valuers and the exit shall be at value not less than average of the two valuations.

control.name: Dual valuation buy-out control
control.description: Appoint two independent valuers, compute the average valuation, and ensure exit price is not below that average.

evidenceSpec.description: Two independent valuation reports and calculation of the average exit value
Buy-out transaction records evidencing exit price

obligations.title: Manager bears responsibility and expenses of exit process
obligations.summary: The responsibility to provide exit to dissenting investors lies with the manager, and expenses for the entire process shall be borne by the manager/sponsor/proposed new manager or sponsor, not charged to unit holders.

clause.excerpt: The responsibility to provide exit to the dissenting investors shall be on the manager. The expenses for the entire process shall be borne by the manager/sponsor/proposed new manager or sponsor and shall not be charged to the unit holders.

control.name: Exit cost allocation control
control.description: Ensure exit process expenses are booked to manager/sponsor accounts and not charged to unit holders.

evidenceSpec.description: Expense allocation records showing exit costs borne by manager/sponsor and not unit holders

obligations.title: Complete exit process within 3 months of dissent window expiry
obligations.summary: The entire exit process for dissenting investors must be completed within 3 months from the date of expiry of the last date of the offer for dissent.

clause.excerpt: The entire process of exit to dissenting investors shall be completed within 3 months from the date of expiry of last date of the offer for dissent.

control.name: Exit timeline tracker
control.description: Track dissent window expiry date and monitor completion of all exits within the 3-month deadline.

evidenceSpec.description: Timeline log of dissent window close and completion dates for each exit

obligations.title: Trustee/sponsor to oversee exit process and update SEBI regularly
obligations.summary: The trustee of the AIF (if a trust) or the sponsor (for any other AIF) is responsible for overseeing the exit process, ensuring compliance, and regularly updating SEBI on developments.

clause.excerpt: The trustee of AIF (in case AIF is a trust)/ sponsor (in case of any other AIF) shall be responsible for overseeing the process, ensuring compliance and regularly updating SEBI on the developments.

control.name: Oversight and SEBI reporting control
control.description: Designate trustee/sponsor oversight of the exit process and maintain periodic SEBI updates on developments.

evidenceSpec.description: SEBI update submissions during the exit process
Oversight meeting minutes or compliance sign-offs by trustee/sponsor

obligations.title: Pay fee within 15 days of effecting change in manager/sponsor or control
obligations.summary: When an AIF effects a proposed change in manager/sponsor or a change in control of manager/sponsor, the prescribed fee must be paid within 15 days of the change taking effect.

clause.excerpt: The aforesaid fee shall be paid within 15 days of effecting the proposed change in manager/sponsor or change in control of manager/sponsor.

control.name: Change-event fee payment control
control.description: Maintain a register of changes in manager/sponsor or changes in control of manager/sponsor. On effecting any such change, trigger a fee payment workflow so the prescribed fee is remitted within 15 days, and record the payment date against the change effective date for monitoring.

evidenceSpec.description: Fee payment confirmation (challan, receipt or bank remittance proof) evidencing payment of the prescribed fee
Register entry comparing the date the change was effected with the date the fee was paid, verifying payment occurred within 15 days

obligations.title: Provide detailed tabular example of fees and charges in PPM with distribution waterfall
obligations.summary: Every AIF must include in its PPM a detailed tabular example showing how fees and charges will apply to the investor, including the distribution waterfall.

clause.excerpt: Every AIF shall, in its PPM provide a detailed tabular example of how the fees and charges shall be applicable to the investor including the distribution waterfall.

control.name: PPM fee disclosure review
control.description: As part of PPM drafting and pre-filing review, compliance verifies that the PPM contains a detailed tabular example of how fees and charges apply to investors, including the distribution waterfall, before the PPM is filed or issued.

evidenceSpec.description: The PPM section containing the detailed tabular example of fees and charges applicable to the investor, including the distribution waterfall
Pre-filing review checklist or sign-off confirming the tabular fee example and distribution waterfall are present in the PPM

obligations.title: Comply with SEBI comments before scheme launch or PPM circulation
obligations.summary: The Merchant Banker/AIF must comply with any comments provided by SEBI during the 30-day review period before launching the scheme or circulating the PPM.

clause.excerpt: Comments, if any, provided by SEBI during this period of 30 days shall be complied with by Merchant Banker/ AIF prior to launch of the scheme/ circulation of PPM.

control.name: SEBI comment resolution gate
control.description: Maintain a tracker of comments received from SEBI during the 30-day review window, assign each comment for remediation, and block scheme launch or PPM circulation until every comment is evidenced as addressed and sign-off is obtained.

evidenceSpec.description: Comment resolution matrix mapping each SEBI comment to the change made in the scheme documents or PPM, with approver sign-off
Final PPM or scheme launch document confirming incorporation of SEBI comments prior to circulation or launch

obligations.title: Submit CA certificate confirming no funds raised
obligations.summary: AIFs that have not raised any funds from investors must submit a certificate from a Chartered Accountant to the effect that no funds have been raised, within 6 months from the end of the financial year.

clause.excerpt: such AIFs shall submit a Certificate from a Chartered Accountant to the effect that no funds have been raised, within 6 months from the end of the Financial Year.

control.name: Annual no-funds-raised certificate filing
control.description: At the end of each financial year, identify AIFs under management that have not raised any funds from investors; for each such AIF, obtain a Chartered Accountant's certificate confirming that no funds have been raised and submit it within 6 months of the financial year end, logging the certificate and submission date.

evidenceSpec.description: Chartered Accountant's certificate stating that no funds have been raised from investors, for the relevant financial year
Submission record or acknowledgment showing the certificate was filed within 6 months of the end of the financial year

obligations.title: Limit joint investors to a maximum of 2 persons
obligations.summary: Where investors are accepted jointly under the permitted relationships (spouse, parent, son or daughter), the AIF must not allow more than 2 persons to act as joint investors.

clause.excerpt: not more than 2 persons shall act as joint- investors in an AIF

control.name: Joint investor count check
control.description: At subscription onboarding, validate that each application under the permitted joint-investor relationships names no more than 2 joint investors; reject or return applications exceeding the cap before acceptance.

evidenceSpec.description: Subscription/onboarding records showing the count of joint investors per accepted application is 2 or fewer
Signed subscription forms or application records for joint-investor applications evidencing the cap was applied

obligations.title: Apply minimum investment amount to each investor in other joint-investor cases
obligations.summary: Where joint investors fall outside the permitted relationships, each such investor must individually meet the minimum investment amount prescribed for the relevant AIF category or sub-category.

clause.excerpt: for every investor, the minimum investment amount, as specified in AIF Regulations for respective category/sub-category of AIF, shall apply

control.name: Per-investor minimum investment validation
control.description: At acceptance, identify joint investors not covered by the permitted relationships and verify each person's individual commitment or contribution meets the category-wise minimum investment amount before acceptance.

evidenceSpec.description: Subscription records showing each non-permitted joint investor's individual amount meets the applicable category minimum
Commitment letters or contribution advices per investor evidencing individual minimum amounts

obligations.title: Ensure each joint investor contributes to the AIF or scheme
obligations.summary: Every person accepted as a joint investor must actually contribute funds towards the AIF or the scheme of the AIF.

clause.excerpt: Each of the joint investor shall contribute towards the AIF/scheme of AIF.

control.name: Joint investor contribution verification
control.description: On receipt of funds, reconcile contributions to confirm each named joint investor has contributed towards the AIF or scheme, and flag any joint investor for whom no contribution is received.

evidenceSpec.description: Contribution reconciliation showing funds received from each named joint investor
Bank statements, remittance advices or contribution receipts attributed to each joint investor

obligations.title: Report overseas limit utilization within 5 working days
obligations.summary: AIFs must report each utilization of the overseas investment limits on the SEBI Intermediary portal within 5 working days of that utilization.

clause.excerpt: AIFs shall report the utilization of the overseas limits within 5 working days of such utilization on SEBI Intermediary portal.

control.name: Overseas limit utilization reporting
control.description: Track every utilization of the overseas investment limits and, for each event, file a utilization report on the SEBI Intermediary portal within 5 working days, with a workflow that flags unreported utilizations approaching the 5-day mark.

evidenceSpec.description: SEBI Intermediary portal submission acknowledgement/receipt for each overseas limit utilization report, timestamped within 5 working days of the utilization
Reconciliation of overseas utilization events against filed reports showing every utilization has a corresponding portal submission dated within 5 working days

obligations.title: Report non-utilisation of overseas limit on expiry of validity period
obligations.summary: If an AIF has not used its SEBI-approved overseas limit within four months of approval, it must report the non-utilisation through the SEBI intermediary portal within 2 working days of the validity period expiring.

clause.excerpt: In case an AIF has not utilized the overseas limit granted to them within a period of four months from the date of SEBI approval (hereinafter referred to as ‘validity period’), the same shall be reported within 2 working days after expiry of the validity period

control.name: Overseas limit validity-period tracker
control.description: Maintain a register of SEBI-approved overseas limits with approval dates and four-month validity expiry dates; on expiry with nil utilisation, trigger filing of the non-utilisation report on the SEBI intermediary portal within 2 working days.

evidenceSpec.description: SEBI intermediary portal filing acknowledgement for non-utilisation of the overseas limit, timestamped within 2 working days of validity period expiry
SEBI approval letter and utilisation records evidencing nil deployment of the overseas limit during the validity period

obligations.title: Report unutilised part of overseas limit on expiry of validity period
obligations.summary: If an AIF has used only part of its overseas limit by the end of the validity period, it must report the unutilised portion through the SEBI intermediary portal within 2 working days of expiry.

clause.excerpt: In case an AIF has not utilized a part of the overseas limit within the validity period, the same shall be reported within 2 working days after expiry of the validity period

control.name: Partial utilisation reconciliation
control.description: Reconcile amounts deployed against the sanctioned overseas limit as the validity period ends; where a part remains unutilised, file the partial non-utilisation report on the SEBI intermediary portal within 2 working days of expiry.

evidenceSpec.description: Portal filing acknowledgement reporting the unutilised portion, submitted within 2 working days of validity period expiry
Utilisation ledger reconciling deployed amounts against the sanctioned overseas limit as at validity period expiry

obligations.title: Report decision to surrender overseas limit within 2 working days
obligations.summary: If an AIF or VCF decides to surrender its overseas limit at any time during the validity period, it must report the surrender through the SEBI intermediary portal within 2 working days of the decision.

clause.excerpt: In case an AIF/ VCF wishes to surrender the overseas limit at any point of time within the validity period, the same shall be reported within 2 working days from the date of decision to surrender the limit.

control.name: Surrender decision reporting
control.description: Log the internal decision to surrender the overseas limit (board or investment committee resolution) and file the surrender report on the SEBI intermediary portal within 2 working days of that decision.

evidenceSpec.description: Board or investment committee resolution recording the decision to surrender the overseas limit, with the decision date
Portal filing acknowledgement of the surrender report submitted within 2 working days of the decision date

obligations.title: Notify existing clients of proposed management change before effecting it
obligations.summary: Following SEBI's prior approval of a change in management, the portfolio manager must inform all existing investors/clients about the proposed change before it takes effect so they can decide whether to continue.

clause.excerpt: the portfolio manager shall inform its existing investors/ clients about the proposed change prior to effecting the same

control.name: Change-in-management client notice workflow
control.description: On receipt of SEBI prior approval for a change in management/control, a workflow generates and dispatches a notice describing the proposed change to every existing investor/client, with a verification gate that blocks effecting the change until dispatch to all clients is confirmed.

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the notice sent to existing investors/clients describing the proposed change in management
Dispatch log showing the notice date to each client precedes the effective date of the management change

obligations.title: Offer exit without exit load with window of at least 30 calendar days
obligations.summary: Along with the change notice, the portfolio manager must give existing investors/clients an option to exit without any exit load, keeping the window open for not less than 30 calendar days from the date of the communication.

clause.excerpt: give an option to exit without any exit load, within a period of not less than 30 calendar days, from the date of such communication

control.name: Exit-option window management
control.description: The client communication and redemption systems are configured so that the change notice states the no-exit-load exit option and the exit window remains open for at least 30 calendar days from the notice date, with exit loads suppressed for exits made within that window.

evidenceSpec.description: Exit-option communication to clients stating the no-exit-load offer and the window dates
Redemption/exit records showing exit load waived for in-window exits and the window spanning at least 30 calendar days from the communication date

obligations.title: Obtain annual self-certification from distributors on Code of Conduct compliance
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager must ensure that each distributor provides a self-certification confirming compliance with the Code of Conduct, received within 15 calendar days of the end of every financial year.

clause.excerpt: within 15 [calendar] days from the end of every financial year, a self-certification is also received from distributors with regard to compliance with Code of conduct

control.name: Distributor Code of Conduct self-certification collection
control.description: Maintain a register of all engaged distributors; circulate the Code of Conduct self-certification template ahead of each financial year end; collect signed self-certifications from every distributor within 15 calendar days of year end; track outstanding items and escalate non-responders.

evidenceSpec.description: Signed Code of Conduct self-certification on file from each distributor for the financial year
Tracker showing self-certifications received from all active distributors within 15 calendar days of financial year end

obligations.title: Ensure distributors of its services are registered with APMI
obligations.summary: Portfolio Managers must ensure that any person or entity engaged to distribute its portfolio management services holds APMI registration obtained in accordance with the criteria laid down by APMI.

clause.excerpt: Portfolio Managers shall ensure that any person or entity engaged in the distribution of its services has obtained registration with APMI, in accordance with the criteria laid down by APMI

control.name: Distributor APMI registration verification
control.description: Maintain a distributor master list; obtain and verify the APMI registration certificate before onboarding any distributor; re-verify registration status against APMI records periodically; do not engage distributors lacking valid APMI registration.

evidenceSpec.description: APMI registration certificate on file for every engaged distributor
Distributor register reconciled against APMI records confirming each engaged distributor holds valid APMI registration

obligations.title: Adopt defined Strategies layer (Equity, Debt, Hybrid, Multi Asset)
obligations.summary: Portfolio Managers must adopt an additional layer of broadly defined investment themes called Strategies, comprising Equity, Debt, Hybrid and Multi Asset, in addition to Investment Approaches.

clause.excerpt: In addition to Investment Approach, an additional layer of broadly defined investment themes called “Strategies” shall be adopted by Portfolio Managers. These broad Strategies shall be ‘Equity’, ‘Debt’, ‘Hybrid’ and ‘Multi Asset’.

control.name: Strategy framework adoption
control.description: Configure the product and benchmarking master so the four defined Strategies (Equity, Debt, Hybrid, Multi Asset) exist as the layer above Investment Approaches, evidenced by an approved policy or system configuration.

evidenceSpec.description: Approved policy or product master extract showing the four Strategies adopted

obligations.title: Tag each Investment Approach to one and only one Strategy
obligations.summary: Every IA must be tagged to one and only one of the defined Strategies. A Portfolio Manager may tag multiple IAs to the same Strategy, and the tagging decision rests with the Portfolio Manager.

clause.excerpt: Each IA shall be tagged to one and only one Strategy from the Strategies as above. This tagging shall be at the discretion of the concerned Portfolio Manager. A Portfolio Manager may tag more than one IA to a Strategy, but each IA must be tagged to only one Strategy.

control.name: IA-Strategy tagging validation
control.description: Maintain a mapping of each Investment Approach to exactly one Strategy and run a validation that blocks any IA left untagged or tagged to more than one Strategy.

evidenceSpec.description: Mapping report showing each IA carries exactly one Strategy tag

obligations.title: Select one prescribed benchmark when tagging an IA to a Strategy
obligations.summary: While tagging an IA to a Strategy, the Portfolio Manager must select one benchmark from those prescribed for that Strategy, so investors can evaluate the relative performance of Portfolio Managers.

clause.excerpt: While tagging an IA to a particular Strategy, the Portfolio Manager shall select one benchmark from those prescribed for that Strategy to enable the investor to evaluate relative performance of the Portfolio Managers.

control.name: Benchmark selection at tagging
control.description: Make the benchmark field mandatory whenever an IA is tagged to a Strategy, restricting choices to the benchmarks prescribed for that Strategy.

evidenceSpec.description: IA records showing a benchmark from the Strategy's prescribed set populated at tagging

obligations.title: Board responsible for appropriate Strategy and benchmark selection
obligations.summary: The Board of the Portfolio Manager is accountable for ensuring that the Strategy and benchmark selected for each IA are appropriate.

clause.excerpt: The Board of the Portfolio Managers shall be responsible for ensuring appropriate selection of Strategy and benchmark for each IA.

control.name: Board oversight of tagging
control.description: Table Strategy and benchmark selections for each IA before the Board for review and approval, and record the outcome in the minutes.

evidenceSpec.description: Board minutes or resolutions evidencing review of Strategy and benchmark selection for each IA

obligations.title: Offer exit without exit load before changing IA tagging
obligations.summary: An IA's Strategy or benchmark tag may be changed only after subscribers are offered an option to exit without any exit load, and the IA's performance track record prior to the change must not be used for performance reporting; this is verified in the annual audit.

clause.excerpt: Once an IA is tagged to a Strategy and/or to a benchmark, the tagging shall be changed only after offering an option to subscribers to the IA to exit without any exit load. The performance track record (of the specific IA whose tagging with Strategy/ benchmark was changed) prior to the change shall not be used by the Portfolio Manager for performance reporting. Further, the same shall be verified as part of annual audit under the Regulations.

control.name: Tagging-change subscriber exit workflow
control.description: Before effecting any change to an IA's Strategy or benchmark tag, issue exit notices without exit load to subscribers, suppress the pre-change track record in performance reporting, and subject both steps to annual audit verification.

evidenceSpec.description: Subscriber notices offering exit without exit load issued prior to the tagging change
Performance reports for the changed IA excluding its pre-change track record

obligations.title: Record Strategy and benchmark changes with justification for annual audit
obligations.summary: Every change in Strategy and/or benchmark must be recorded with proper justification, and such records are verified as part of the annual audit under the Regulations.

clause.excerpt: The changes in Strategy and/ or benchmark shall be recorded with proper justification and shall be verified as part of the annual audit under the Regulations.

control.name: Strategy change register
