control.description: Log each Strategy or benchmark change in a register with written justification and provide the register to the annual auditor for verification.

evidenceSpec.description: Change register entries with justification plus the annual audit verification report

obligations.title: Update Disclosure Document and website within 7 calendar days of material changes
obligations.summary: Whenever there is a material change in the information already disclosed, the Portfolio Manager must update the Disclosure Document and upload the revised version on its website within 7 calendar days.

clause.excerpt: Portfolio Managers shall ensure that any material changes in the above information is updated in the Disclosure Document and uploaded on their respective websites within 7 [calendar] days.

control.name: Material change disclosure update control
control.description: Maintain a register of the information currently contained in the Disclosure Document; when a material change is identified, route the revised Disclosure Document through compliance review, publish it on the firm's website, and log the change date and upload date to evidence the 7 calendar-day window.

evidenceSpec.description: The revised Disclosure Document as published on the Portfolio Manager's website, with the webpage upload timestamp visible
Change log comparing the date each material change was identified with the date the updated Disclosure Document was uploaded, evidencing a gap of 7 calendar days or less

obligations.title: Provide MITC document to client and obtain client acknowledgement
obligations.summary: The Portfolio Manager must give each client a Most Important Terms and Conditions (MITC) document, prepared in the standard format prescribed by APMI in consultation with SEBI, and obtain the client's due acknowledgement of it.

clause.excerpt: Portfolio Manager shall additionally provide to its client a “Most Important Terms and Conditions (MITC)” document, which shall be duly acknowledged by the client.

control.name: MITC issuance and acknowledgement control
control.description: Add a mandatory step to the client onboarding checklist to generate the MITC from the APMI-prescribed standard format, deliver it to the client, and capture and store the client's signed or otherwise duly acknowledged MITC on the client record.

evidenceSpec.description: The client-acknowledged MITC document held on file for each client
Client-master check confirming that an MITC issuance and client acknowledgement is recorded for every active client

obligations.title: Audit firm-level performance data annually
obligations.summary: Portfolio Managers must have their firm-level performance data audited once every year.

clause.excerpt: The firm-level performance data of Portfolio Managers shall be audited annually.

control.name: Annual performance data audit
control.description: Engage an independent auditor to audit firm-level performance data each financial year and retain the audit report and management responses.

evidenceSpec.description: Signed audit report covering firm-level performance data for the financial year

obligations.title: Report paragraph 4.5.3 compliance confirmation to SEBI annually
obligations.summary: Within sixty days of the end of each financial year, the Portfolio Manager must report to SEBI confirming compliance with paragraph 4.5.3 of the Master Circular.

clause.excerpt: Confirmation of compliance with paragraph 4.5.3 of this Master Circular shall be reported to SEBI within sixty [calendar] 74days of end of each financial year.

control.name: Annual SEBI compliance confirmation filing
control.description: Prepare a report confirming compliance with paragraph 4.5.3, have it reviewed, and submit it to SEBI within 60 days of each financial year end.

evidenceSpec.description: Compliance confirmation report filed with SEBI along with the filing acknowledgment
Filing timestamp recorded within 60 days of the end of the financial year

obligations.title: Certify SEBI compliance report by Directors/Partners or authorized persons
obligations.summary: The report submitted to SEBI must be certified by the Directors or Partners of the Portfolio Manager, or by person(s) authorized by the Board of Directors/Partners.

clause.excerpt: The said report to SEBI shall be certified by the Directors/Partners of the Portfolio Manager or by person(s) authorized by the Board of Directors/Partners of the Portfolio Manager.

control.name: Authorized signatory certification
control.description: Maintain board authorization for persons empowered to certify the SEBI report and obtain the certification signature before the report is filed.

evidenceSpec.description: Certified report bearing the signature of Directors/Partners or board-authorized persons, together with the board authorization record

obligations.title: Submit annual audit compliance confirmation to SEBI within 60 days of FY end
obligations.summary: Within sixty calendar days of the end of each financial year, the Portfolio Manager must submit to SEBI a confirmation of compliance with the annual audit of firm-level performance data conducted in line with APMI's standard ToR.

clause.excerpt: Portfolio Managers shall submit the confirmation of compliance with the requirement of annual audit of firm-level performance data in line with the standard ToR specified by APMI, to SEBI within sixty [calendar] days from the end of each financial year.

control.name: Annual audit compliance filing
control.description: Maintain an annual compliance calendar that triggers the audit of firm-level performance data against APMI's standard ToR, prepares the confirmation of compliance, routes it for authorised certification, and files it with SEBI within sixty calendar days of financial year end.

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the confirmation of compliance submitted to SEBI with submission acknowledgement, dated within sixty calendar days of financial year end
Annual audit report on firm-level performance data prepared in line with the standard ToR specified by APMI

obligations.title: Certify compliance report by Directors/Partners or authorised persons
obligations.summary: The confirmation report filed with SEBI must be certified by the Directors/Partners of the Portfolio Manager, or by person(s) authorised by the Board of Directors/Partners.

clause.excerpt: The aforesaid report on confirmation of compliance to SEBI shall be certified by Directors/ Partners of the Portfolio Manager or by person(s) authorized by the Board of Directors/Partners of the Portfolio Manager.

control.name: Authorised sign-off on compliance report
control.description: Before filing, verify the report carries certification from Directors/Partners or from person(s) authorised by the Board of Directors/Partners, and retain the authorisation records on file.

evidenceSpec.description: Signed certification page of the compliance report identifying the certifier and their capacity
Board of Directors/Partners authorisation for the certifying person(s), where the certifier is not a Director/Partner

obligations.title: Due diligence per SFA standards before availing QIB benefits for concentrated schemes
obligations.summary: For every AIF scheme where an investor, or investors belonging to the same group, contribute 50 percent or more of the scheme corpus, the AIF manager must carry out the necessary due diligence as per the implementation standards formulated by SFA before the scheme avails benefits available to QIBs under ICDR Regulations and other SEBI Regulations.

clause.excerpt: necessary due diligence as per the implementation standards formulated by SFA, shall be carried out prior to availing benefits available to QIBs under ICDR Regulations and other SEBI Regulations.

control.name: Pre-QIB-benefit due diligence gate
control.description: Before the scheme avails any benefit designated for QIBs, compute the contribution of each investor and of investors belonging to the same group to the scheme corpus; where any such concentration is 50 percent or more, complete the due diligence prescribed by the SFA implementation standards and record sign-off confirming completion prior to availing the QIB benefit.

evidenceSpec.description: Per-scheme corpus contribution schedule showing each investor's contribution percentage and aggregated same-group percentages, flagging schemes where concentration is 50 percent or more
Due diligence report and supporting records prepared in line with the SFA implementation standards, with compliance sign-off dated prior to the scheme availing QIB benefits

Register of instances where the scheme availed benefits available to QIBs under ICDR Regulations or other SEBI Regulations, each mapped to a completed due diligence record where the 50 percent concentration trigger applied

obligations.title: Carry out due diligence per SFA implementation standards for in-scope AIF schemes
obligations.summary: For every AIF scheme whose manager or sponsor is an entity regulated by RBI, or which has RBI-regulated investors meeting the 25 percent corpus, associate, or investment-committee voting-control criteria, the necessary due diligence under the implementation standards formulated by SFA must be carried out.

clause.excerpt: necessary due diligence as per the implementation standards formulated by SFA, shall be carried out

control.name: Scheme classification and SFA due diligence
control.description: Classify every scheme against the para 20.5.1(a) criteria (RBI-regulated manager or sponsor; RBI-regulated investor individually or with same-group investors contributing 25 percent or more of corpus; RBI-regulated associate of the manager/sponsor; or RBI-regulated majority or veto power over the investment committee) and, where the scheme qualifies, complete and document the due diligence prescribed by the SFA implementation standards before investments are made.

evidenceSpec.description: Due diligence report for each in-scope scheme mapping the checks performed to the SFA implementation standards and recording findings on each qualifying criterion
Scheme register flagging each scheme that meets an RBI-link criterion together with due diligence completion status and date

obligations.title: Carry out look-through criteria check for AIF/offshore fund investors
obligations.summary: Where an investor in an in-scope scheme is itself an AIF, or a fund set up outside India or in an International Financial Services Centre in India, the check for whether investors are regulated by RBI must be performed on a look-through basis rather than at the immediate investor level.

clause.excerpt: If an investor of the scheme is an AIF, or a fund set up outside India or in International Financial Services Centres in India, then the criteria check for investor(s) regulated by RBI shall be carried out on a look through basis

control.name: Look-through review of AIF and offshore fund investors
control.description: For each investor that is an AIF or a fund set up outside India or in an IFSC in India, trace its investor or ownership chain to identify RBI-regulated entities at the underlying level and apply the 25 percent corpus, associate and voting-power tests to that look-through population before concluding the investor criteria check.

evidenceSpec.description: Investor records for each AIF, offshore or IFSC fund investor documenting the look-through chain and the RBI-regulated status determination of underlying investors
Look-through analysis worksheet or underlying investor declaration supporting the criteria check conclusion

obligations.title: Block investments creating prohibited indirect exposure for RBI-regulated lenders
obligations.summary: For schemes covered by para 20.5.1(a), the manager must ensure the scheme makes no investment that would lead an RBI-regulated lender/entity to acquire or hold, indirectly through the AIF scheme, an interest or exposure in the investee company that it is not permitted to acquire or hold directly.

clause.excerpt: the manager shall ensure that the scheme does not make any investment that would lead to the RBI regulated lender/entity acquiring or holding an interest/exposure in the investee company indirectly (that is, through investment in a scheme of an AIF), that they are not permitted to acquire or hold directly

control.name: Pre-investment indirect exposure screen
control.description: Before each scheme investment is approved or deployed, assess whether it would give any RBI-regulated lender/entity connected to the scheme an indirect interest or exposure in the investee company that RBI norms do not permit it to acquire or hold directly; if so, block the investment and record the rationale.

evidenceSpec.description: Pre-investment compliance log showing the indirect-exposure screen result (cleared or blocked) for every scheme investment
Investment committee minutes or compliance sign-off evidencing that approved investments create no prohibited indirect exposure for RBI-regulated lenders/entities

obligations.title: Pre-investment due diligence for land-border investor corpus
obligations.summary: For every AIF scheme where 50 percent or more of the corpus is contributed by investors, or their beneficial owners, who are citizens of/from/situated in a country sharing a land border with India, the necessary due diligence per the SFA implementation standards must be completed before making any investment.

clause.excerpt: necessary due diligence as per the implementation standards formulated by SFA, shall be carried out prior to making any investment

control.name: Land-border investor due diligence gate
control.description: Before executing any investment, the AIF manager computes the share of scheme corpus contributed by investors and beneficial owners from land-border countries; where it is 50 percent or more, the SFA implementation-standard due diligence is completed and cleared before the investment is made.

evidenceSpec.description: Due diligence report/clearance prepared per SFA implementation standards, dated prior to the investment for schemes with 50 percent or more land-border corpus.
Investor register and beneficial-ownership screening records showing country flags and the 50 percent corpus computation for each scheme.

obligations.title: Report qualifying investments to custodian within 30 days
obligations.summary: After completing the due diligence, the scheme must report to its custodian, within 30 days of the investment, details of any investment that would result in holding 10 percent or more of the equity/equity-linked securities of the investee company on a fully-diluted basis, in the SFA-specified format.

clause.excerpt: such scheme shall report details of its investment, which would result in the scheme holding 10 percent or more of equity/equity-linked securities issued by an investee company (on a fully-diluted basis), to its custodian within 30 days of investment

control.name: Qualifying investment reporting to custodian
control.description: Track investments that would result in 10 percent or more holding of the investee company's equity/equity-linked securities on a fully-diluted basis, complete the due diligence, and submit the report in the SFA-specified format to the custodian within 30 days of the investment date.

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the investment report submitted to the custodian in the SFA-specified format, with submission date within 30 days of the investment.
Log of investments meeting the 10 percent fully-diluted threshold mapped to report submission dates evidencing the 30-day window.

obligations.title: Respond to CTR observations within 15 days
obligations.summary: When the trustee/sponsor intimates observations or comments on the CTR, the manager must make the necessary changes to the CTR and submit its reply to the trustee/sponsor within 15 days of receiving those observations.

clause.excerpt: Within 15 days from the date of receipt of such observations/comments, the manager shall make necessary changes in the CTR, as may be required, and submit its reply to the trustee/sponsor.

control.name: CTR observation response tracking
control.description: Log the date observations/comments on the CTR are received from the trustee/sponsor, assign owners to make the required changes to the CTR, draft and approve the reply, and submit it to the trustee/sponsor, tracking completion against the 15-day window from receipt of the observations.

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the revised CTR and the manager's reply submitted to the trustee/sponsor, showing submission within 15 days of receipt of the observations/comments
Intake log entry recording the date observations/comments were received from the trustee/sponsor, the computed 15-day due date, and the actual reply submission date falling within the window

obligations.title: Mention registration number in all correspondence
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager must state its certificate of registration number in every piece of correspondence it sends to SEBI, other authorities, stock exchanges, and its clients.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio manager shall mention its registration number contained in the certificate of registration in all the correspondence with SEBI, other authorities, Stock Exchanges and the clients of the portfolio manager.

control.name: Registration number in outbound correspondence templates
control.description: Maintain standard templates for all outbound letters, emails and notices to SEBI, other authorities, stock exchanges and clients that automatically carry the portfolio manager's certificate of registration number, and verify each outgoing communication displays the number before dispatch.

evidenceSpec.description: Samples of outbound correspondence to SEBI, other authorities, stock exchanges and clients showing the registration number on each item
Template review report confirming every approved correspondence template includes the certificate of registration number

obligations.title: Designate a senior officer as Compliance Officer
obligations.summary: The Portfolio Manager must appoint a senior officer to the role of Compliance Officer to oversee compliance with all Rules, Regulations, Guidelines and Notifications issued by SEBI, the Government of India and other regulatory authorities.

clause.excerpt: the Portfolio Manager shall designate a senior officer as compliance Officer

control.name: Compliance Officer designation
control.description: Senior management formally appoints a senior officer as Compliance Officer, recording the designation with defined seniority, reporting lines and responsibility for regulatory compliance oversight.

evidenceSpec.description: Board or senior management approval / appointment letter designating the named senior officer as Compliance Officer

obligations.title: Compliance Officer to co-ordinate with regulators and ensure internal compliance
obligations.summary: The designated Compliance Officer must co-ordinate with regulatory authorities on various matters, provide necessary guidance, and ensure compliance internally within the firm.

clause.excerpt: who shall co-ordinate with regulatory authorities in various matters and provide necessary guidance as also ensure compliance internally

control.name: Regulatory liaison and internal compliance process
control.description: A defined process by which the Compliance Officer serves as the point of contact for regulator communications, disseminates regulatory guidance internally, and monitors day-to-day adherence to applicable rules and regulations.

evidenceSpec.description: Log of regulatory correspondence and co-ordination handled by the Compliance Officer
Internal compliance guidance circulars or advisories issued by the Compliance Officer to staff

obligations.title: Ensure SEBI-observed deficiencies do not recur
obligations.summary: The Compliance Officer must ensure that observations made and deficiencies pointed out by SEBI in the functioning of the portfolio manager are remediated and do not recur.

clause.excerpt: The Compliance Officer shall inter alia ensure that the observations made / the deficiencies pointed out by SEBI in the functioning of the portfolio managers do not recur

control.name: Regulatory deficiency tracker
control.description: A deficiency register in which every SEBI observation or inspection finding is recorded, assigned a corrective action with an owner, tracked to closure, and re-tested periodically to confirm the deficiency has not recurred.

evidenceSpec.description: Deficiency register mapping each SEBI observation to corrective action, closure status and recurrence check
Compliance Officer's periodic report to senior management confirming remediation of SEBI observations and absence of recurrence

obligations.title: SEBI correspondence only via principal office, not branch offices
obligations.summary: All correspondence with SEBI relating to registration and clarifications on SEBI Guidelines/Circulars must be sent exclusively by the portfolio manager's principal office; branch offices must not make such correspondence.

clause.excerpt: Correspondence relating to registration and clarifications on Guidelines / Circulars issued by SEBI shall be made only by the principal office of the portfolio manager and not by any of its branch offices.

control.name: Principal-office correspondence routing
control.description: Maintain a policy and routing mechanism that directs all SEBI registration and clarification correspondence through the principal office, with checks to prevent branch offices from sending such correspondence directly to SEBI.

evidenceSpec.description: Correspondence policy or board-approved procedure designating the principal office as the sole authorised channel for SEBI registration and clarification correspondence
Outgoing correspondence log showing that all SEBI-directed registration and clarification letters originate from the principal office address and none from branch offices

obligations.title: Have a code of conduct under PIT Regulations
obligations.summary: Portfolio managers must have a code of conduct as envisaged under the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015.

clause.excerpt: The portfolio managers shall have a code of conduct as envisaged under the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015.

control.name: Insider trading code of conduct adoption
control.description: Adopt and maintain a code of conduct conforming to the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015, approved by management and made applicable to all employees and designated persons.

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the adopted code of conduct with evidence of board or management approval and version history.
Check that the code of conduct document references the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 and is acknowledged by all covered persons.

obligations.title: Apply online to SEBI for prior approval via SEBI Intermediary Portal
obligations.summary: The Portfolio Manager must submit its application for prior approval to SEBI electronically through the SEBI Intermediary Portal. The application must be made online at the specified portal rather than by any other channel.

clause.excerpt: An online application shall be made by Portfolio Manager to SEBI for prior approval through the SEBI Intermediary Portal (https://siportal.sebi.gov.in).

control.name: Prior approval application submission control
control.description: When the firm requires SEBI prior approval, a responsible officer prepares and files the application online through the SEBI Intermediary Portal (siportal.sebi.gov.in), verifies the submission is acknowledged, and tracks it through to receipt of approval before the underlying activity is undertaken.

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the online application as filed on the SEBI Intermediary Portal, together with the portal acknowledgement/receipt and any SEBI approval communication

obligations.title: File change-in-control approval application with SEBI before NCLT filing
obligations.summary: When a portfolio manager seeks approval for a proposed change in control, the application under the PM Regulations must be filed with SEBI before the application is filed with the NCLT.

clause.excerpt: The application seeking approval for the proposed change in control under PM Regulations shall be filed with SEBI prior to filing the application with NCLT;

control.name: SEBI-first filing sequence for change in control
control.description: Operate a pre-filing checkpoint so that the change-in-control approval application is completed and submitted to SEBI, with the SEBI acknowledgment captured, before the NCLT application is submitted; the NCLT filing is gated on evidence of the earlier SEBI filing.

evidenceSpec.description: SEBI filing acknowledgment or submission receipt for the change-in-control application, showing the filing date
Copy of the NCLT application with its filing date, demonstrating the SEBI filing preceded it

obligations.title: File NCLT application within three-month validity of in-principle approval
obligations.summary: The in-principle approval remains valid for three months from its date of issue, and the relevant application must be made to NCLT within that window.

clause.excerpt: The validity of such in-principle approval shall be three months from the date of such approval, within which the relevant application shall be made to NCLT;

control.name: In-principle approval validity tracker
control.description: On receipt of an in-principle approval, log the approval date, compute the three-month expiry, prepare the NCLT application, and file it with NCLT before the approval lapses.

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the in-principle approval communication showing its date of issue
NCLT application filing receipt or acknowledged copy showing the filing date falls within three months of the approval date

obligations.title: Principal officer and fund management decision-makers to pass NISM-Series-XXI-B exam
obligations.summary: The associated persons functioning as principal officer of a Portfolio Manager, and employees with decision-making authority related to fund management, must obtain certification from the National Institute of Securities Markets by passing the NISM-Series-XXI-B: Portfolio Managers Certification Examination.

clause.excerpt: shall obtain certification from the National Institute of Securities Markets by passing the NISM- Series-XXI-B: Portfolio Managers Certification Examination

control.name: Certified personnel register
control.description: Maintain a register of the principal officer and all employees with fund management decision-making authority, verifying that each holds a valid NISM-Series-XXI-B certification before assuming or continuing in the role, and re-verify whenever such personnel change.

evidenceSpec.description: Copies of NISM-Series-XXI-B certification certificates for the principal officer and each employee with fund management decision-making authority
HR/personnel record check confirming every individual in a fund management decision-making role holds the NISM-Series-XXI-B certification

obligations.title: Follow prescribed format for calculation of Net worth
obligations.summary: Portfolio Managers must calculate Net worth in the prescribed format, i.e. a statement of networth based on audited or unaudited accounts as on a specified date.

clause.excerpt: Following format shall be followed by Portfolio Managers for calculation of Net worth

control.name: Net worth statement format control
control.description: Whenever Net worth is computed, the firm prepares the statement of networth strictly in the prescribed format, based on audited or unaudited accounts as on the relevant date, and the prepared statement is reviewed for format conformity before use or submission.

evidenceSpec.description: Statement of networth prepared in the prescribed format based on audited / unaudited accounts as on the stated date

obligations.title: PMS distributor associated persons must pass NISM-Series-XXI-A certification exam
obligations.summary: Associated persons engaged by a Portfolio Manager as distributors of Portfolio Management Services must obtain certification from the National Institute of Securities Markets by passing the NISM-Series-XXI-A PMS Distributors Certification Examination.

clause.excerpt: shall obtain certification from the National Institute of Securities Markets by passing the NISM-Series-XXI-A: Portfolio Management Services (PMS) Distributors Certification Examination

control.name: Distributor certification verification
control.description: Before engaging or continuing any associated person as a distributor of Portfolio Management Services, the Portfolio Manager verifies that the person holds NISM-Series-XXI-A certification and retains a copy of the pass certificate on record.

evidenceSpec.description: Copy of the NISM-Series-XXI-A PMS Distributors Certification Examination pass certificate for each associated person engaged as a PMS distributor

obligations.title: Segregate each client's funds and securities from own funds and securities
obligations.summary: Each client's funds and portfolio of securities must be kept separately from the portfolio manager's own funds and securities, as mandated by the PM Regulations.

clause.excerpt: the portfolio manager shall segregate each client’s funds and portfolio of securities and keep them separately from his own funds and securities

control.name: Client asset segregation
control.description: Maintain segregated accounts and ledger records so that every client's funds and securities are held distinctly from the portfolio manager's proprietary funds and securities, with regular reconciliation to confirm no commingling occurs.

evidenceSpec.description: Segregation reconciliation report evidencing client funds and securities balances held separately from the portfolio manager's own balances

obligations.title: Ensure safekeeping of clients' funds and securities
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager is responsible for the safekeeping of all client funds and securities held on behalf of clients.

clause.excerpt: be responsible for safekeeping of clients’ funds and securities

control.name: Client asset safekeeping
control.description: Operate custody and safeguarding arrangements for client funds and securities, including access controls, authorised-signatory oversight, and periodic verification that client holdings are intact and accounted for.

evidenceSpec.description: Custody and safekeeping records together with periodic client holdings verification statements

obligations.title: Maintain clear segregation of each client's funds via back office records
obligations.summary: Each client's funds must be clearly segregated, which is to be achieved through proper and clear maintenance of back office records.

clause.excerpt: There shall be a clear segregation of each client’s fund through proper and clear maintenance of back office records,

control.name: Client fund segregation in back office records
control.description: Operate back office accounting so that every client's funds are maintained in separate, clearly identifiable records with no commingling between clients, and periodically review record-keeping to confirm segregation remains clear and proper.

evidenceSpec.description: Back office records/ledgers demonstrating separate fund accounting for each client
Check that back office records show per-client fund segregation with no cross-client commingling

obligations.title: Maintain short-term liquid fund deployments in line with paragraph 2.2.2
obligations.summary: Portfolio Managers must ensure that any short-term deployment of funds in Liquid Mutual Funds for cash management, pending investment of funds, is maintained in accordance with paragraph 2.2.2 of the Master Circular.

clause.excerpt: any short term deployment of funds in Liquid Mutual Funds for the purpose of cash management shall be maintained on the lines as per paragraph 2.2.2 of this Master Circular.

control.name: Liquid fund deployment compliance check
control.description: Operate a pre-deployment validation and periodic review ensuring every short-term investment in Liquid Mutual Funds made for cash management while funds await deployment conforms to the conditions prescribed in paragraph 2.2.2 of the Master Circular.

evidenceSpec.description: Register of all short-term Liquid Mutual Fund deployments showing purpose (cash management, pending investment) and parameters evidencing conformity with paragraph 2.2.2 conditions
Internal cash-management policy for deployment in liquid funds aligned to paragraph 2.2.2 of the Master Circular

obligations.title: Provide clients an option to be on-boarded directly without distribution intermediaries
obligations.summary: Portfolio Managers must offer clients the option of being on-boarded directly, with no intermediation by persons engaged in distribution services.

clause.excerpt: Portfolio Managers shall provide an option to clients to be on-boarded directly, without intermediation of persons engaged in distribution services.

control.name: Direct onboarding option in client onboarding workflow
control.description: The client onboarding process includes a documented channel through which a client may elect to be on-boarded directly by the Portfolio Manager, without any person engaged in distribution services intermediating, and this option is presented to every prospective client.

evidenceSpec.description: Onboarding policy or account opening form capturing the direct onboarding option offered to clients and the client's election of onboarding mode.
Onboarding records showing that clients were offered the direct onboarding option and instances of direct onboarding completed without distributor involvement.

obligations.title: Disclose direct on-boarding option in disclosures, marketing material and website
obligations.summary: Portfolio Managers must prominently disclose, in their Disclosure Documents, marketing material and on their website, the availability of the option for direct on-boarding.

clause.excerpt: Portfolio Managers shall prominently disclose in its Disclosure Documents, marketing material and on its website, about the option for direct on-boarding.

control.name: Direct on-boarding disclosure control
control.description: Maintain a review process ensuring that every edition of the Disclosure Document, every piece of marketing material, and the website prominently carry the disclosure of the direct on-boarding option, with sign-off before publication and periodic checks that the disclosure remains present and prominent.

evidenceSpec.description: Current Disclosure Document evidencing the prominent disclosure of the direct on-boarding option
Specimens of marketing material showing the direct on-boarding option disclosure
Website scan or capture showing the prominent direct on-boarding option disclosure

obligations.title: Put in place a written policy on team roles in managing client funds and securities
obligations.summary: Portfolio Managers must adopt a written policy, compliant with the PM Regulations and circulars issued thereunder, detailing the specific activities, roles and responsibilities of teams engaged in fund management, dealing, compliance, risk management and back-office functions with regard to client funds and securities, including order placement, execution and trade allocation amongst clients.

clause.excerpt: which inter-alia detail the specific activities, role and responsibilities of various teams engaged in fund management, dealing, compliance, risk management, back-office, etc., with regard to management of client funds and securities including the order placement, execution of order, trade allocation amongst clients and other related matters.

control.name: Written fund management policy
control.description: Draft, approve and maintain a written policy that maps each team (fund management, dealing, compliance, risk management, back-office) to its specific activities, roles and responsibilities for handling client funds and securities, expressly covering order placement, order execution and allocation of trades amongst clients, and keep the policy aligned with the PM Regulations and related SEBI circulars.

evidenceSpec.description: Approved written policy document detailing team-wise activities, roles and responsibilities for management of client funds and securities, including order placement, execution and trade allocation amongst clients
Approval or sign-off record evidencing adoption of the policy and its mapping to the PM Regulations and circulars issued thereunder

obligations.title: Put in place a specific policy compliant with PM Regulations
obligations.summary: Portfolio Managers must establish a specific policy in compliance with the PM Regulations and the circulars issued thereunder. The policy must, among other things, provide for the matters enumerated in the following provisions.

clause.excerpt: Portfolio Managers shall also put in place a specific policy, in compliance with the PM Regulations and circulars issued thereunder

control.name: Policy establishment and alignment control
control.description: Draft, approve, and operationalise a firm-level specific policy covering the matters required by the PM Regulations and related circulars, with periodic review to ensure continued alignment with those regulations and circulars.

evidenceSpec.description: The specific policy document approved by the firm's governing body, evidencing coverage of the PM Regulations and circulars issued thereunder.
Policy register entry showing the policy is in force, dated, and mapped to the relevant PM Regulations and circulars.

obligations.title: Obtain prior written PO and Compliance Officer approval for deviations
obligations.summary: Any deviation must arise from exigency only and requires prior written approval of the Portfolio Manager's Principal Officer and Compliance Officer, supported by a detailed rationale.

clause.excerpt: Deviations, if any, shall be on account of exigency only and require prior written approval of the Principal Officer and Compliance officer of the Portfolio Manager with a detailed rationale for such deviation.

control.name: Prior written deviation approval workflow
control.description: Before implementing any deviation, route a request with detailed rationale to the Principal Officer and Compliance Officer; record their prior written approvals before proceeding.

evidenceSpec.description: Prior written approval from Principal Officer and Compliance Officer with detailed rationale for the exigency-based deviation

obligations.title: Obtain Board approval of policies specified in paragraphs 2.6.1 & 2.6.2
obligations.summary: The policies required under paragraphs 2.6.1 and 2.6.2 must be approved by the Board or equivalent body of the Portfolio Manager before they take effect.

clause.excerpt: The aforesaid policies as mentioned at paragraphs 2.6.1 & 2.6.2 shall be approved by the Board / equivalent body of the Portfolio Manager.

control.name: Board approval of policies
control.description: Route the policies required under paragraphs 2.6.1 and 2.6.2 to the Board or equivalent governing body for formal approval, record the approval as a resolution in the board minutes, and retain the approved policy documents.

evidenceSpec.description: Board or equivalent body meeting agenda, minutes, and resolution recording approval of the policies referenced in paragraphs 2.6.1 & 2.6.2, together with the approved policy documents.

obligations.title: Treat all clients in a fair and equitable manner
obligations.summary: Portfolio Managers must ensure that every client is treated fairly and equitably, without preference or discrimination, and must comply with the fair-treatment requirements set out in the items that follow this paragraph.

clause.excerpt: Portfolio Managers shall ensure that all clients are treated in a fair and equitable manner

control.name: Client fair-treatment policy
control.description: Maintain a documented fair-treatment policy governing allocation of investment opportunities, fee charging, transaction handling and reporting so that all clients receive uniform treatment; monitor client activity against the policy and investigate any instance of preferential or disadvantageous treatment.

evidenceSpec.description: Board or compliance-approved client fair-treatment policy document
Exception report evidencing that no client received preferential or disadvantageous treatment relative to the fair-treatment policy

obligations.title: Constitute a dealing team for order placement and execution
obligations.summary: Portfolio Managers must set up a dealing team that is responsible for placing and executing all orders in line with the firm's own policies. The team may optionally include the Principal Officer or the person appointed under Regulation 7(2)(e) of the PM Regulations.

clause.excerpt: Portfolio Managers shall constitute a dealing team (DT) which shall be responsible for order placement and execution of all orders in accordance with the aforesaid policies of the Portfolio Manager.

control.name: Dealing team constitution
control.description: Formally designate a dealing team (with named members, which may include the Principal Officer or the Regulation 7(2)(e) appointee) and assign it sole responsibility for order placement and execution in accordance with the firm's dealing policies.

evidenceSpec.description: Internal policy or organisational note constituting the dealing team, listing its members and their responsibility for order placement and execution

obligations.title: Conduct all DT conversations only via recorded lines or authorized email ids
obligations.summary: All conversations of DT must take place exclusively through the dedicated recorded telephone lines or through emails sent from authorized email ids. No other channel of conversation is permitted.

clause.excerpt: All conversations of DT shall be only through the dedicated recorded telephone lines or through emails from authorized email ids.

control.name: Approved communication channel enforcement
control.description: Maintain a register of dedicated recorded telephone lines and authorized email ids for DT, restrict DT users to only these channels, and monitor call recordings and email logs to detect and block conversations through any other line or email id.

evidenceSpec.description: Call log and voice-recording coverage report showing every DT conversation took place on the dedicated recorded telephone lines
Email log extract showing all DT emails were sent only from the authorized email ids

obligations.title: Prohibit mobile phones and other communication devices inside the dealing room
obligations.summary: The firm must ensure that mobile phones and any communication devices other than the recorded telephone lines are not permitted inside the dealing room, and operate entry controls to enforce this prohibition.

clause.excerpt: Mobile phones or any other communication devices other than the recorded telephone lines shall not be allowed inside the dealing room.

control.name: Dealing room device entry control
control.description: Maintain a standing prohibition on mobile phones and other communication devices in the dealing room: provide device deposit lockers or collection points at entry points, display signage, conduct periodic physical sweeps and spot checks of the dealing room, and record any exceptions with remediation.

evidenceSpec.description: Periodic sweep log of the dealing room confirming no mobile phones or non-recorded communication devices were present during dealing hours
Device deposit register or locker records evidencing collection of mobile phones at the dealing room entrance, along with the written dealing room device policy

obligations.title: Restrict internet access in dealing room to trade-execution activities only
obligations.summary: Portfolio managers must restrict internet access on computers and other devices inside the dealing room, permitting its use solely for activities related to trade execution.

clause.excerpt: Access to internet facilities on computers and other devices inside the dealing room shall be restricted and shall only be used for activities related to trade execution.

control.name: Dealing room internet access restriction
control.description: Operate a network-level restriction (e.g., firewall/allowlist configuration) on all computers and devices located inside the dealing room so that internet access is available only for trade-execution related activities, and monitor usage to detect and remediate any non-execution internet use.

evidenceSpec.description: Dealing room IT/network access policy and firewall configuration records showing internet access restrictions on dealing room computers and devices
Periodic review of internet access logs from dealing room devices confirming usage is confined to trade execution activities

obligations.title: Restrict dealing room entry/access to authorized employees only
obligations.summary: The Portfolio Manager must ensure that only employees designated as authorized in its own policies may enter or access the dealing room.

clause.excerpt: Entry/access to the dealing room shall be restricted to authorized employees as defined in the aforementioned policies of the Portfolio Manager.

control.name: Dealing room access control
control.description: Maintain a documented list of authorized employees per the PM's policies; enforce physical and electronic access restrictions to the dealing room (access cards, biometric or key control, visitor prohibition); update the authorized list on joinings, exits and role changes; periodically reconcile entry logs against the authorized list and escalate any unauthorized access.

evidenceSpec.description: Dealing room access policy and the current list of authorized employees it defines
Dealing room entry/access logs reconciled against the authorized employee list, showing no entries by non-authorized personnel

obligations.title: No sharing of information except for approved trade execution
obligations.summary: Portfolio Managers must not share information through any mode; the only permitted exception is sharing for trade execution carried out under the approved policies of the Portfolio Manager.

clause.excerpt: There shall be no sharing of information through any mode, except for trade execution under the approved policies of the Portfolio Manager.

control.name: Information sharing prohibition control
control.description: Operate channel monitoring and data-loss-prevention controls across all communication and data-transfer modes to block information sharing, with an allow-list limited to trade execution flows defined in the approved policies of the Portfolio Manager.

evidenceSpec.description: Monitoring logs of communication and data-transfer channels showing no information sharing outside the approved trade execution exception
Approved policies of the Portfolio Manager defining the permitted trade execution information flows

obligations.title: Automated funds and securities management system for AUM of INR 1000 crores or more
obligations.summary: Portfolio Managers managing INR 1000 crores or more under discretionary and non-discretionary services must operate an automated system, with minimal manual intervention, for effective funds and securities management, including order management and allocation of securities to each client.

clause.excerpt: Portfolio Managers with assets under management of INR 1000 crores or more under discretionary and non-discretionary services, shall have in place an automated system with minimal manual intervention for ensuring effective funds and securities management including order management and allocation of securities to each client.

control.name: Automated funds and securities management platform
control.description: Operate and maintain an automated system with minimal manual intervention that covers funds and securities management, order management, and allocation of securities to each client, applied whenever discretionary and non-discretionary AUM reaches INR 1000 crores or more.

evidenceSpec.description: System documentation describing the automated funds and securities management workflow, including order management and client-level allocation modules
Screenshots or walkthrough of the live automated system showing order capture and allocation of securities to individual clients
Sample order and allocation records demonstrating automated, minimally manual processing across clients

obligations.title: System must capture pre-order and final trade allocation details with deviations
obligations.summary: The portfolio manager's system must clearly record, for trades, the client-wise allocation determined before order placement as well as the final allocation to clients, along with any instances of deviation between the two.

clause.excerpt: The aforesaid system shall inter-alia clearly capture details with respect to pre-order placement allocation as well as final allocation of trades to clients along with instances of deviation, if any, as mentioned at paragraph 2.6.2.4 above.

control.name: Pre- and post-trade allocation logging control
control.description: Operate an order and trade management system that, for every trade, logs the client-wise allocation determined prior to order placement and the final allocation actually executed, automatically flags and records any deviation between the intended and final allocations, and retains these records for review and reporting.

evidenceSpec.description: Extract a sample of executed trades from the system showing, per trade, the recorded pre-order placement allocation, the final client allocation, and any flagged deviation instances between them.

obligations.title: Comply with the Cybersecurity and Cyber Resilience Framework (CSCRF)
obligations.summary: All portfolio managers must comply with the applicable provisions of the Cybersecurity and Cyber Resilience Framework for SEBI Regulated Entities specified in SEBI circular SEBI/HO/ITD-1/ITD_CSC_EXT/P/CIR/2024/113 dated August 20, 2024, along with any subsequent directions issued on the subject.

clause.excerpt: All Portfolio Managers shall comply with the applicable provisions of Cybersecurity and Cyber Resilience Framework (CSCRF) for SEBI Regulated Entities (REs), specified vide SEBI Circular no. SEBI/HO/ITD- 1/ITD_CSC_EXT/P/CIR/2024/113 dated August 20, 2024, including any subsequent directions in this regard.

control.name: CSCRF compliance programme
control.description: Operate a firm-wide cybersecurity and cyber resilience programme that implements the applicable CSCRF controls under the August 20, 2024 circular, tracks subsequent SEBI directions on the framework, and reviews implementation status against the framework's requirements.

CSCRF compliance status report or self-assessment submissions made to SEBI/regulatory systems as required by the circular

obligations.title: Value portfolio debt and money market securities per APMI standardized norms
obligations.summary: Portfolio managers must carry out valuation of all portfolio debt and money market securities in accordance with the standardized valuation norms prescribed by APMI, which mirror the corresponding Mutual Fund norms.

clause.excerpt: Valuation of the portfolio debt and money market securities by portfolio managers shall be carried out in accordance with these standardized valuation norms prescribed by APMI.
